page: Vultr voc-g-4c-16gb-80s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the system allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier at 3435.28. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores falling into the average category. Memory performance is characterized by an average read-only bandwidth of 144.89 GB/sec for large blocks and a strong write bandwidth of 113.87 GB/sec. Single-threaded operations perform well, as evidenced by strong gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput are relatively weak.

This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, single-threaded processing tasks, and moderate database operations. While it handles small-scale language model inference adequately, processing larger models like a 7B parameter model results in poor to weak performance. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores offer reliable compute resources, making it a cost-efficient option for applications requiring consistent CPU performance without the overhead of high-end memory or storage arrays.
